newsitem.title: UK: British fashion chain to stop buying from Burma.
newsitem.headline: British fashion chain to stop buying from Burma.

text.p: British fashion retailer Burton Group Plc said on Thursday it will stop buying merchandise from Burma in response to pressure from customers.
The company, the number two clothing retailer in Britain behind Marks and Spencer Plc, said it had instructed its suppliers in the Far East to terminate all contracts by the end of the year.
"This decision has been taken following a review of customer opinion towards merchandise sourced from Burma," Burton said in a statement.

A spokeswoman said merchandise, mostly textiles, from Burma represented less than one percent of the group's business. She said it was the first time Burton had taken such action, but the company had become aware of customer opinion about the country, which has been widely criticised for its record on human rights.
Human rights and labour groups have alleged that Burma's military government has forced millions on its citizens into forced labour.
The United States last month virtually banned new investment in the country by U.S. citizens or businesses.
